skill.name: allra-database-schema
skill.description: Guides Allra backend development with JPA entity patterns, QueryDSL repository conventions, DTO projections, transaction boundaries, and relationship mappings.
skill.summary: Apply consistent JPA, QueryDSL, repository, and transaction patterns in Allra Spring applications.
skill.author: Allra-Fintech

security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, QueryDSL fetch operations, and ordinary Java domain methods. A separate high-severity issue remains because the examples assign a supplied password directly to an entity without demonstrating hashing.

remediation.issue: The user creation examples pass and assign a raw password without showing one-way password hashing.
remediation.suggestion: Hash passwords with an approved adaptive password encoder before persistence, and revise the entity example to store only the resulting password hash.

content.user_title: Design Reliable JPA and QueryDSL Data Layers
content.value_statement: Inconsistent persistence patterns create fragile repositories, transaction errors, and inefficient entity relationships. This skill applies Allra standards to JPA, QueryDSL, and Spring transactions.
actual_capabilities: Structures JPA repositories with optional QueryDSL support interfaces and implementation classes.
Builds QueryDSL projections with records and @QueryProjection.
Places queries according to their primary From entity.
Applies read-only or writable @Transactional annotations to service methods.
Defines JPA entities with identifiers, columns, auditing fields, and controlled constructors.
Maps lazy entity relationships with cascade and orphan-removal guidance.
limitations: The guidance targets Java 17, Spring Boot 3.2, JPA, Hibernate, and optional QueryDSL.
It does not design database migrations, indexes, constraints, or production deployment procedures.
Database-specific functions still require verification against the selected database and version.
The password example requires security correction before use in production.

use_cases.title: Create a New Persistence Model
use_cases.description: Generate a JPA entity, repository, relationships, and transaction-aware service methods for a new domain feature.

use_cases.title: Standardize QueryDSL Repositories
use_cases.description: Review repository placement, support interfaces, predicates, and DTO projections against Allra conventions.

use_cases.title: Audit Transaction Boundaries
use_cases.description: Classify service operations as read-only or writable and identify missing @Transactional declarations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a JPA Entity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a JPA entity for [domain object] with these fields: [fields]. Apply the Allra entity and relationship conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting a simple persistence model.

prompt_templates.title: Add a QueryDSL Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Create QueryDSL repository support for [entity] to filter by [conditions] and return [DTO fields]. Explain the repository placement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when adding filtered database reads.

prompt_templates.title: Review Transactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these service methods: [methods]. Assign suitable @Transactional settings and explain which methods must remain writable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when checking service transaction boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Persistence Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this persistence layer: [design]. Check QueryDSL ownership, projections, transaction boundaries, lazy relationships, and database compatibility. List unresolved risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a comprehensive architecture review.

output_examples.input: Review a user search repository that queries users by email and name.
output: Keep the query under the user repository because User is the primary From entity.
Use nullable BooleanExpression predicates for optional email and name filters.
Return a dedicated summary projection instead of loading complete entities.

output_examples.input: Choose transaction settings for list, create, and activate service methods.
output: Mark list operations as read-only transactions.
Use writable transactions for create and activate operations.
Declare the transaction annotation explicitly on each public service method.

output_examples.input: Review an order-to-user and order-to-items mapping.
output_examples.output: Use lazy loading for the user association. Maintain both sides when adding items, and confirm cascade deletion matches business requirements.

best_practices: Verify generated mappings and queries against the active database engine and version.
Use repository interfaces from services and keep implementation classes behind those interfaces.
Hash credentials before persistence and never copy raw password examples into production.
anti_patterns: Do not inject QueryDSL implementation classes directly into services.
Do not mark write operations as read-only transactions.
Do not use eager relationships or broad cascades without validating access and deletion behavior.

faq.question: Which technology versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Java 17 or later, Spring Boot 3.2 or later, and JPA with Hibernate.

faq.question: Is QueryDSL required?
faq.answer: No. QueryDSL and its support-interface pattern are optional when another repository approach fits the project.

faq.question: Where should a QueryDSL query be defined?
faq.answer: Place it in the repository for the primary entity named in the query From clause.

faq.question: When should readOnly be enabled?
faq.answer: Use readOnly for methods that only query data. Use a writable transaction when any persistent state can change.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee database portability?
faq.answer: No. Verify functions, pagination, and generated SQL against the selected database engine and version.

faq.question: Can I use the password example unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Hash passwords with an approved adaptive encoder before persistence, and store only the resulting hash.
